newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan bank note issue limit to rise to 51 trln yen.
newsitem.headline: Japan bank note issue limit to rise to 51 trln yen.

text.p: Japan will increase its issuing limit on bank notes by 3.8 trillion yen to 51 trillion yen, effective from December 20, a Finance Ministry official said on Tuesday.
The decision was made at a morning cabinet meeting.
An official at the Bank of Japan said the lifting of the limit was in response to increasing demand for bank notes, partly for bonus payments, ahead of the year-end.
Without such a measure, there was a risk that bank notes would have had to be issued beyond the current ceiling of 47.2 trillion yen, she said.
Money traders said the BOJ's move had little significance on the money policy front, but had certain implications for the state of the economy.
Seasonal fund demand typically seen at the end of the year is expected to strengthen from December 20, leading the BOJ to raise the previous ceiling.
Also, due to longer-than-usual New Year holidays, such fund demand is stronger this year, traders said.
Strong demand for cash also suggested that economic activities, particularly consumption, may have started to pick up, albeit mildly, traders said.
Year-end bonus payments by Japanese companies may be bigger than previously expected, they said.

"The move by the central bank implied that some economic activities are picking up, though modestly, and individual consumption is recovering. But it is premature to judge that the overall economic recovery is firming markedly," said Shoji Kitta, managing director of Tokyo Tanshi Co Ltd, the largest money broker in Japan.
He added that purchases by consumers ahead of a planned consumption tax increase due in April may have played a part in the recovery in personal consumption.
Japan's consumption tax is scheduled to be raised to five percent in April from the current three percent.
The issue limit was last revised upward on December 15 last year, by 3.3 trillion yen to 47.2 trillion yen.
The BOJ is due to announce November money supply growth at 2350 GMT on Tuesday.
